note: Open '[Device]:' requests that cannot be modelled yet, with the exact field the vendor does not publish. Rendered into docs/DEVICE_REGISTRY.md by scripts/regen-registry-doc.js - edit this file, then run: npm run regen:registry-doc

requests.missing: the whole port layout: the SKU is not in Ubiquiti's own cloud-gateway index (sixteen cards, `udw-pro` occurs zero times), `techspecs.ui.com/unifi/cloud-gateways/udw-pro` redirects to the site root and `store.ui.com/.../udw-pro` answers 404. The published datasheet `dl.ui.com/ds/udw_ds.pdf` is the non-Pro Dream Wall.
requests.unblock: a Ubiquiti page, datasheet or quick-start guide that names UDW-PRO's ports and PoE budget. Modelling it from the non-Pro numbers is the family-sibling error this catalogue has already corrected.

requests.missing: front-end port count per node. The V200R001C20 data sheet (4-slide pptx) and the product page both stop at port *types* - `16/32/64 Gb FC, 10/25/40/100 GbE` - because the count is a function of the controllers and interface cards ordered.
requests.unblock: a controller/interface-card configuration, or an ordering guide that pins ports per base model. The same field is missing for #743.

requests.missing: per-model interface-module configuration: which slots take front-end modules and how many ports each module type has. The slot half is vendor-sourced (white paper: twelve hot-swappable IOMs per enclosure, six slots per controller); the port half is not. The books that carry it (`EDOC1100368229` / `EDOC1100368230` Product Description, `EDOC1100305240` / `EDOC1100305243` Hardware Installation Guide) are only served section-by-section and their section slugs are not indexed.
requests.unblock: one section URL from either Product Description, or a stated configuration (e.g. "X8100 with a 4-port 10GE electrical module in IOM 0 and IOM 1"). X8100 and X9100 are different enclosures and get separate specs.

requests.missing: the service-board part number valid in an E6616X subrack, and that board's front-panel census. The E6600 generation publishes its board list only inside the closed hedex tree.
requests.unblock: the board set to be modelled (e.g. "E6616X with two TN13LSC"), or one section URL from the E6600 board chapter.

requests.missing: the client-side port census of a service board valid in the E9605. The frame-to-board matrix is no longer the gap: `TNG2DAP` section 1.9 "Valid Slots" (vendor PDF, read 2026-11-17) gives E9605 = IU1-IU5, E9612 = IU1-IU13, E9624 = IU1-IU24, with IU6/IU7/IU18/IU19 unusable in 1:3 mode. What is still missing is one CLIENT board chapter: every indexed e-file chapter is an optical-layer board (TNG2DAP is a 5x LC EDFA), and `TNG1N206` / `TNG1N210` / `TNG1M*` chapters are not indexed on e.huawei.com or e-file.huawei.com.
requests.unblock: one `TNG1N*` or `TNG1M*` chapter PDF, or a stated configuration plus that board's Port Specifications table (e.g. "E9605 with 5x TNG1N210"). The board names print their own port counts - "TNG1N210: 10 x 10 Gbit/s line service processing board" - so the board half is one document away while the frame half is already sourced.

requests.missing: the same client board chapter (`TNG1N*` / `TNG1M*`). The frame half is vendor-sourced: E9612 = IU1-IU13 in `TNG2DAP` section 1.9, and the family specification table gives 13 service slots with `Cross-connect Type: NA`, so the slot count is mode-independent for this frame - unlike its E9624 sibling.
requests.unblock: one client board chapter (`TNG1N*` / `TNG1M*` Port Specifications), or a stated configuration on a board whose chapter exists. No protection mode is needed: 13 slots either way.

requests.missing: the same client board chapter (`TNG1N*` / `TNG1M*`), plus the protection mode, which decides the port count: 1:1 gives 12 large or 24 small slots, 1:3 gives 10 or 20, and IU6/IU7/IU18/IU19 are unusable in 1:3. The frame arithmetic itself is settled and vendor-sourced (`TNG2DAP` section 1.9 and the E9600 family brochure).
requests.unblock: one client board chapter plus the protection mode to model (1:1 or 1:3). With both, the product is a stated card complement - `E9624 (24x <board>)` - and needs no guessing.
